passages.text: After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.
passages.sermon:
Saul died.
David was a leader and a warrior.
David fought the Amalekites and defeated them.
David returned from this battle.
David stayed in the town of Ziklag.
He remained there for two days.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְדָוִ֣ד שָׁ֔ב מֵהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־ הָעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב דָּוִ֛ד בְּצִקְלָ֖ג יָמִ֥ים שְׁנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.
passages.sermon:
On the third day, a man came from Saul’s camp.
His clothes were torn.
He had dust on his head.
He arrived where David was.
He fell to the ground before David.
He bowed down to show respect.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וְהִנֵּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ בָּ֤א מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וּבְגָדָ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיְהִי֙ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: “Where have you come from?” David asked. “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader of Israel.
David spoke to the man.
David asked, "Where have you come from?"
The man answered David.
The man said, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּב֑וֹא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִמְלָֽטְתִּי׃

passages.text: “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.” “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
A man came to David from Saul’s camp.
David spoke to the man.
David asked, “What happened?”
David said, “Please tell me.”
The man answered David.
He said, “The people ran away from the battle.”
He said, “Many people fell.”
He said, “Many people died.”
He said, “Saul is dead.”
He said, “Jonathan, Saul’s son, is also dead.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו דָּוִ֛ד מֶה־ הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַגֶּד־ נָ֣א לִ֑י וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֲשֶׁר־ נָ֨ס הָעָ֜ם מִן־ הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְגַם־ הַרְבֵּ֞ה נָפַ֤ל מִן־ הָעָם֙ וַיָּמֻ֔תוּ וְגַ֗ם שָׁא֛וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ מֵֽתוּ׃

passages.text: Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
A young man brought David a report.
David spoke to the young man.
David asked the young man a question.
David said, “How do you know?”
David asked, “How do you know that Saul is dead?”
David also asked, “How do you know that Jonathan, Saul’s son, is dead?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד אֶל־ הַנַּ֖עַר הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֑וֹ אֵ֣יךְ יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־ מֵ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל וִיהֽוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.
passages.sermon:
A young man brought a report to David.
He said, “I was on Mount Gilboa.”
I saw Saul there.
Saul was leaning on his spear.
Chariots were coming close to Saul.
Horsemen were also coming close to Saul.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הַנַּ֣עַר׀ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֗וֹ נִקְרֹ֤א נִקְרֵ֙יתִי֙ בְּהַ֣ר הַגִּלְבֹּ֔עַ וְהִנֵּ֥ה שָׁא֖וּל נִשְׁעָ֣ן עַל־ חֲנִית֑וֹ וְהִנֵּ֥ה הָרֶ֛כֶב וּבַעֲלֵ֥י הַפָּרָשִׁ֖ים הִדְבִּקֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: When he turned around and saw me, he called out and I answered, ‘Here I am!’
passages.sermon:
Saul turned around.
Saul saw me.
Saul called out to me.
I answered him.
I said, "Here I am."
passages.original: וַיִּ֥פֶן אַחֲרָ֖יו וַיִּרְאֵ֑נִי וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֵלָ֔י וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: ‘Who are you?’ he asked. So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
passages.sermon:
Saul was the first king of Israel.
Saul was wounded and near death on Mount Gilboa.
An Amalekite man found Saul.
Saul saw the Amalekite.
Saul spoke to the Amalekite.
Saul asked, "Who are you?"
The Amalekite answered Saul.
The Amalekite said, "I am an Amalekite."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֖י מִי־ אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָ֔יו עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to me.
He was Saul, the king of Israel.
He was wounded and suffering.
He said, "Stand over me."
He said, "Kill me."
He said, "Agony has seized me."
He said, "My life still lingers in me."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י עֲמָד־ נָ֤א עָלַי֙ וּמֹ֣תְתֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֲחָזַ֖נִי הַשָּׁבָ֑ץ כִּֽי־ כָל־ ע֥וֹד נַפְשִׁ֖י בִּֽי׃

passages.text: So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”
passages.sermon:
I am an Amalekite.
I stood over the man.
I killed him.
I knew he could not live after he had fallen.
I took the crown from his head.
I took the band from his arm.
I brought the crown and the band here to you, my lord.
passages.original: וָאֶעֱמֹ֤ד עָלָיו֙ וַאֲמֹ֣תְתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֣י יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽחְיֶ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֣י נִפְל֑וֹ וָאֶקַּ֞ח הַנֵּ֣זֶר׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ רֹאשׁ֗וֹ וְאֶצְעָדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ זְרֹע֔וֹ וָאֲבִיאֵ֥ם אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David heard about the death of Saul and Jonathan.
David felt deep sorrow.
David grabbed his own clothes.
David tore his clothes.
All the men who were with David saw this.
All the men with David also tore their clothes.
passages.original: וַיַּחֲזֵ֥ק דָּוִ֛ד בִּבְגָדוֹ וַיִּקְרָעֵ֑ם וְגַ֥ם כָּל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
passages.sermon:
David and his men heard that Saul and Jonathan had died in battle.
They also learned that many people of Israel had died.
David and his men mourned for them.
They wept for them.
They fasted until evening.
They did this for Saul.
They did this for Jonathan, Saul’s son.
They did this for the people of the LORD.
They did this for the house of Israel.
They mourned because these people had fallen by the sword.
passages.original: וַֽיִּסְפְּדוּ֙ וַיִּבְכּ֔וּ וַיָּצֻ֖מוּ עַד־ הָעָ֑רֶב עַל־ שָׁא֞וּל וְעַל־ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְעַל־ עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ וְעַל־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י נָפְל֖וּ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ס

passages.text: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?” “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
A young man brought David a report.
David spoke to the young man.
David asked, “Where are you from?”
The young man answered David.
He said, “I am the son of a foreigner.”
He said, “I am an Amalekite.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל־ הַנַּ֙עַר֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֶּן־ אִ֛ישׁ גֵּ֥ר עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to the young Amalekite man.
David said, “You killed Saul, the LORD’s anointed king.”
David asked, “Why were you not afraid?”
David said, “You were not afraid to raise your hand against the LORD’s chosen one.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֚יךְ לֹ֣א יָרֵ֔אתָ לִשְׁלֹ֙חַ֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ לְשַׁחֵ֖ת אֶת־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David called for one of his young men.
David spoke to the young man.
David said, “Go. Strike him.”
The young man obeyed David.
The young man struck the Amalekite.
The Amalekite died.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֗ד לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וַיֹּ֖אמֶר גַּ֣שׁ פְּגַע־ בּ֑וֹ וַיַּכֵּ֖הוּ וַיָּמֹֽת׃

passages.text: For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’ ”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to the Amalekite.
David said, "You are responsible for your own death."
Your blood is on your own head.
You said with your own mouth, 'I killed the LORD’s anointed.'"
Your words have testified against you.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד דָּמֶיךָ עַל־ רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פִ֗יךָ עָנָ֤ה בְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָנֹכִ֥י מֹתַ֖תִּי אֶת־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan, and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David mourned for Saul and Jonathan.
Saul was the former king.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
David spoke a song of sorrow about them.
David told the people of Judah to learn this song.
This song is called the Song of the Bow.
The Song of the Bow is written in the Book of Jashar.
The song says, “Israel’s glory lies dead on your hills.”
The song says, “How the mighty have fallen!”
passages.original: וַיְקֹנֵ֣ן דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־ הַקִּינָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את עַל־ שָׁא֖וּל וְעַל־ יְהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ׃ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְלַמֵּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֖ה קָ֑שֶׁת הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל־ סֵ֥פֶר הַיָּשָֽׁר׃ הַצְּבִי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַל־ בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָ֑ל אֵ֖יךְ נָפְל֥וּ גִבּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
passages.sermon:
David spoke these words as a lament for Saul and Jonathan.
David addressed the people of Israel.
David said, “Do not tell this news in Gath.
Do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon.
If you do, the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice.
The daughters of the uncircumcised will exult.”
passages.original: אַל־ תַּגִּ֣ידוּ בְגַ֔ת אַֽל־ תְּבַשְּׂר֖וּ בְּחוּצֹ֣ת אַשְׁקְל֑וֹן פֶּן־ תִּשְׂמַ֙חְנָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּֽן־ תַּעֲלֹ֖זְנָה בְּנ֥וֹת הָעֲרֵלִֽים׃

passages.text: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David mourned for Saul and Jonathan.
David spoke a lament.
David addressed the mountains of Gilboa.
He said, “Mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew.
May you have no rain.
May your fields not yield grain for offerings.
On your slopes, the shield of the mighty was defiled.
The shield of Saul was defiled there.
Saul’s shield was no longer anointed with oil.”
passages.original: הָרֵ֣י בַגִּלְבֹּ֗עַ אַל־ טַ֧ל וְאַל־ מָטָ֛ר עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וּשְׂדֵ֣י תְרוּמֹ֑ת כִּ֣י שָׁ֤ם נִגְעַל֙ מָגֵ֣ן גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים מָגֵ֣ן שָׁא֔וּל בְּלִ֖י מָשִׁ֥יחַ בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was a mighty warrior.
Saul was a mighty warrior.
Jonathan used a bow in battle.
Saul used a sword in battle.
Jonathan’s bow did not turn back from the blood of the slain.
Jonathan’s bow did not turn back from the fat of the mighty.
Saul’s sword did not return empty.
Saul’s sword always struck down his enemies.
passages.original: מִדַּ֣ם חֲלָלִ֗ים מֵחֵ֙לֶב֙ גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים קֶ֚שֶׁת יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן לֹ֥א נָשׂ֖וֹג אָח֑וֹר וְחֶ֣רֶב שָׁא֔וּל לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם׃

passages.text: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
passages.sermon:
Saul and Jonathan were beloved.
They were delightful in their lives.
They did not separate in death.
They were swifter than eagles.
They were stronger than lions.
passages.original: שָׁא֣וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֗ן הַנֶּאֱהָבִ֤ים וְהַנְּעִימִם֙ בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם וּבְמוֹתָ֖ם לֹ֣א נִפְרָ֑דוּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֣ים קַ֔לּוּ מֵאֲרָי֖וֹת גָּבֵֽרוּ׃

passages.text: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.
passages.sermon:
The daughters of Israel are the women of the nation of Israel.
Saul was the first king of Israel.
Saul gave the daughters of Israel fine clothing.
He clothed them in scarlet.
He gave them luxury.
He put ornaments of gold on their garments.
Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul.
passages.original: בְּנוֹת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־ שָׁא֖וּל בְּכֶ֑ינָה הַמַּלְבִּֽשְׁכֶ֤ם שָׁנִי֙ עִם־ עֲדָנִ֔ים הַֽמַּעֲלֶה֙ עֲדִ֣י זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל לְבוּשְׁכֶֽן׃

passages.text: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was a mighty warrior.
Jonathan fought bravely in battle.
Jonathan died on the heights.
The mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle.
Jonathan lies slain on your high places.
passages.original: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבֹּרִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן עַל־ בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָֽל׃

passages.text: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
passages.sermon:
David speaks.
David mourns for Jonathan.
Jonathan was David’s brother and friend.
David feels deep sorrow for Jonathan.
Jonathan brought David great joy.
Jonathan’s love for David was wonderful.
Jonathan’s love for David was greater than the love of women.
passages.original: צַר־ לִ֣י עָלֶ֗יךָ אָחִי֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נָעַ֥מְתָּ לִּ֖י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְלְאַ֤תָה אַהֲבָֽתְךָ֙ לִ֔י מֵאַהֲבַ֖ת נָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”
passages.sermon: The mighty men have fallen.\r\nThe weapons of war have perished.
passages.original: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבּוֹרִ֔ים וַיֹּאבְד֖וּ כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃פ
